cause: Function-local torch imports: a helper hoisted to module scope lost the local import and only failed at call time, inside training, after the GPU was hot.
fix: Keep the import inside the five functions that need it (the pattern sdm_for_mask already used) and let phase4seg_preflight import every module before any launch.

cause: The Drive FUSE mount dropping I/O mid-step. Every instance is a path under /content/drive: training reads thousands of small tile files straight off the mount, and FUSE returns EIO under that sustained pattern. Not a pipeline defect and not reproducible from the code — the same step succeeds on a re-run.
fix: Re-run the step. To stop it recurring, stage tiles to local NVMe for the epoch rather than reading them per-batch off the mount (CLAUDE.md 3.9 is the same lesson on the write side). Never treat an EIO as evidence about the data. WRITE-SIDE PROBES (2026-09-09): bb50_2011s_cor05 died at epoch A17 on `dest.exists()` inside common.py::_publish_replace, the copy already done and the checkpoint safe on NVMe (phase4_semantic_finetune_train_2011s_2026-09-09 T09-03.log). The exists/stat probes on the publish path now go through common.py::_probe_retry — EIO and ENOTCONN only, 5 tries, 2..30 s backoff, one log line per retry — so a single mount hiccup on a metadata call no longer ends a train step; a mount still refusing after ~1 min raises the original EIO. The READ side (tiles off the mount) is unchanged by that fix.
notes: Mechanism inferred from the errno + the /content/drive path on all five, not from an instrumented reproduction. The 2026-09-09 instance is the one with a traceback naming the exact call (common.py line 750, `dest.exists()`).

cause: The Colab exec handle died mid-step — handle mortality, not a pipeline defect. The VM usually keeps working; only the channel is gone.
fix: Never kill a runtime on a dead handle. Re-attach and read the lake-side log to find out whether the work actually finished.

cause: --infer-aoi named an AOI file the VM could not see: _aoi_pixel_rects reads the path at inference time, so a missing or mis-named AOI kills the step after the model is already loaded. Both instances were launches whose AOI had not been uploaded to the lake.
fix: Preflight every launch-time path VM-side before the queue starts. Same class as the of_2017k failures, where imagery existed only on the local mirror.

signature: '<path>' not recognized as being in a supported file format.
cause: A tile written to the mount was truncated by a partial/interrupted write, so a later step opened a file that exists and has a name but no readable header.
fix: Delete the affected tile directory and re-tile — do not attempt to salvage. This is the same rerun-on-contamination rule as the staged-TIF failure above.

cause: A staged scratch-cache payload vanished between stage() handing it out and the caller opening it (RasterioIOError on /content/phase4_scratch/<file>__<hex>.tif, wb50_2016_in05 inference 2026-09-09T22-09). step_inference stages the CHM lazily from its 8 reader threads; the 6.4 MB CHM is under STAGE_LOCK_MIN_BYTES so the P11.4 lock was a nullcontext, and every scratch-cache guard is keyed by PID, so the threads were invisible to each other: at least two judged "miss" (the log proves K >= 2 — same-label ticks collapse to one line; 7 of 8 when reproduced on the dev box), copied, and each unlinked the canonical name ahead of its own os.replace — deleting the file a sibling thread had just been handed. The process was alone on the VM and reserve() had run before the CHM was staged, so no peer and no evictor was involved; the staged entry was pinned by its own pid throughout.
fix: scratchcache.stage() now holds a process-local per-key lock for its whole body (same-key threads serialise: first copies, rest hit), _clear_destination refuses under ANY live pin (own pid included), and the publish is a bare atomic os.replace with no unlink ahead of it. Gates: qc/test_scratch_cache.py, the "ONE PROCESS, MANY THREADS" section (fail on the pre-fix code). Re-run the arm.
notes: The signature is what harvest_failures.normalise() produces — it swallows the /content path through its trailing colon — not the raw log text; the match is pinned against the real message by qc/test_run_context.py ::test_the_scratch_cache_enoent_signature_is_diagnosed. Distinct from the quoted "'<path>'$" entry above (a missing --infer-aoi file). LIMIT: after normalisation a vanished /content/drive/... source produces this SAME signature, so a future Drive-side ENOENT would be diagnosed as this fixed entry — open the example log and check the path is under /content/phase4_scratch before trusting the match.

signature: Read failed. See previous exception for details.
cause: A rasterio read that failed for a reason recorded in the PRECEDING exception — this row is the wrapper, not the fault. Its example log pairs with the ZIPDecode family above.
fix: Read the exception immediately above it in the log; do not diagnose this line.

signature: edmonds_canopy_mask_2009_trend8_2009__a0cb2778.tif: TIFFReadDirectory:Failed to read directory at offset <n>
cause: postproc read back a mask it had just staged, and the staged TIF was truncated because the previous arm left the scratch dir dirty and the write raced its own reader. The recut1 VM died this way and took its logs with it.
fix: Write logs to the lake, not the VM, and clear /content/phase4_scratch between arms in the payload chain. Re-run the affected arm; the artifact is not salvage.
notes: rerun-on-contamination — never salvage an ambiguous raster
